objectives.statement: Distinguish a variable, coefficient and constant in a practical rule.
Evaluate an expression with correct operation order and units.
Solve and verify a simple linear equation.
Explain why an equation operation must preserve equality.
Identify a valid function without confusing repeated outputs with conflicting outputs.
Interpret function notation and calculate an output.
Identify input restrictions before evaluating a rule.
Find the outputs produced by a stated domain.
Calculate and interpret slope from two coordinates.
Distinguish an intercept change from a slope change.
Connect slope sign to increasing or decreasing outputs.
Interpret a weighted-input prediction without assuming prior ML knowledge.
Apply exponent rules and reject their misuse for sums.
Distinguish constant-ratio exponential change from linear change.
Calculate repeated proportional decay.
Explain e through an increasingly frequent compounding example.
Use a logarithm as the inverse exponent question.
Distinguish common and natural logarithms.
Explain real-log input and base restrictions.
Interpret log sums and negative-log costs without building an algorithm.
Predict horizontal translation using the inside argument.
Separate vertical scale/reflection and translation.
Evaluate composition in the correct order.
Recognize a nonlinear relationship from unequal output changes.
Calculate vector magnitude.
Add corresponding vector components.
Interpret a negative scalar multiplication.
Distinguish magnitude from direction, including the zero vector.
Calculate a signed weighted dot product.
Interpret perpendicular alignment and length effects.
Calculate a projection onto a coordinate direction.
Preserve feature meaning when positions change.
Determine the result shape of a rectangular matrix-vector product.
Compute a row of a rectangular batch prediction.
Diagnose a missing weight without deleting information.
Interpret dataset axes and tensor vocabulary.
Check inner dimensions and output shape.
Compute a matrix product cell by a row-column sum.
Recognize that multiplication order changes shape or validity.
Reject incompatible matrix multiplication.
Map a vector using matrix columns and row sums. (essential)
Interpret rotation and reflection as linear mappings. (essential)
Calculate a shear without confusing it with translation. (essential)
Interpret right-to-left transformation composition. (essential)
Recognize dependent columns and their representable span. (essential)
Construct a standard-basis representation. (introductory)
Distinguish number of columns from rank and dimension. (essential)
Explain what makes a basis for the plane. (essential)
Recognize when an inverse-as-undo cannot exist. (essential)
Use identity and undo a supported scaling. (essential)
Interpret determinant sign and area scaling. (introductory)
Choose numerically appropriate fitting methods and distinguish near-singularity. (essential)
Interpret a known eigenvalue on a preserved direction. (introductory)
Distinguish the zero input from a zero eigenvalue. (introductory)
Recognize that a real eigenbasis is not guaranteed. (introductory)
Connect covariance eigenpairs to PCA without treating arbitrary transforms as PCA. (introductory)
For (t²−1)/(t−1), what is the limit as t approaches 1? (essential)
A function equals −1 to the left of 0 and +1 at and to the right of 0. Does a two-sided limit exist at 0? (essential)
A symmetric difference gives 0 for |t| at 0. What can you conclude? (essential)
Which relationship is valid at a point? (essential)
For g(x,y)=x²+3y², what is ∂g/∂x at (1,2)? (essential)
For the same g, what is ∂g/∂y at (1,2)? (essential)
For q=(x+y)² at (1,2), use (x,y)−0.1∇q(x,y) with both partials from the original point. What is the new y? (essential)
At (1,2), what is the directional derivative of g along the positive x unit direction [1,0]? (essential)
For s(x,y)=x²−y² at (0,0), the gradient is zero. Is this necessarily a local minimum? (essential)
What does a partial derivative with respect to x measure? (essential)
F(x,y)=[x+y,xy]. At (1,2), what is Jacobian entry (output 2, input 1)? (introductory)
For g=x²+3y², what is the Hessian entry ∂²g/∂y²? (introductory)

legacyPilot.risk: Historical coarse transfer objective and 4/5 scorer remain unchanged; per-rule independent granularity is a later pedagogical-audit risk, not a claim of exhaustive rule mastery.

modules.title: Mathematics integration practice
modules.summary: Small cross-topic transfer scenario, not a seventh subject or aggregate mastery assessment.

lessons.title: A prediction is not yet evidence of learning
lessons.summary: Algebra → Linear Algebra → Calculus → Probability → Statistics → Optimization

experiments.title: Fictional house prediction and one-step sensitivity

modules.title: Optimization Foundations
modules.summary: Loss geometry, gradients, simultaneous updates, finite-run diagnostics, penalties and honest evaluation.

lessons.title: Losses, objectives and gradients
lessons.summary: Review functions, squared errors and Calculus partial derivatives. A gradient lists sensitivities at one parameter state.

lessons.title: Gradient updates and learning rates
lessons.summary: Review vectors and scalar multiplication. Compute all gradient components before changing any parameter.

lessons.title: Landscape geometry and scaling
lessons.summary: Review contour maps, coordinate directions and Statistics standardization. Equal coordinate steps need not have equal effects.

lessons.title: Finite-run progress and numerical stability
lessons.summary: Review the update rule and iteration-0 convention. A finite trace is evidence about the inspected states, not an infinite sequence.

lessons.title: Regularization and the objective tradeoff
lessons.summary: Review sums, derivatives and validation splits. A penalty changes what is being minimized.

lessons.title: Honest optimization and ML decisions
lessons.summary: Review sampling, leakage and held-out data. Training success is not the same claim as predictive generalization.

lessons.title: Independent Optimization mastery
lessons.summary: 24 items, 80% and all critical gates; deterministic alternate retry.

modules.title: Statistics Foundations
modules.summary: Summaries, spread, causal reasoning, sampling and honest ML interpretation.

lessons.title: Understanding data
lessons.summary: An observation is one case. Review fractions and Probability sample spaces; no calculus is needed.

lessons.title: Measures of central tendency
lessons.summary: Review sorting, addition and division. Dataset provenance matters before calculating a summary.

lessons.title: Variability and spread
lessons.summary: Review mean, squared differences and square roots. State whether the data describe a population or a sample.

lessons.title: Distributions and visualization
lessons.summary: Review Probability mass/density and quartiles. A chart must state its units, bins and population.

lessons.title: Relationships without causal shortcuts
lessons.summary: Review paired observations and standard deviation. Association and intervention answer different questions.

lessons.title: Sampling and inference
lessons.summary: Review populations, representative sampling and Probability distributions. Approximate inference needs assumptions.

lessons.title: Statistics in machine learning
lessons.summary: Review spread, correlation and sampling. Revisit the preserved Linear Regression lessons for full model training.

lessons.title: Independent Statistics mastery
lessons.summary: 28 items, 80% and all critical gates; deterministic alternate retry.

modules.title: Probability Foundations
modules.summary: Uncertainty, events, conditional probability, Bayes, distributions and probabilistic ML interpretation.

lessons.title: Understanding probability
lessons.summary: Fractions are part ÷ whole. A percentage is a fraction out of 100.

lessons.title: Counting and multiple events
lessons.summary: Review outcomes and complements first. The denominator counts equally likely outcomes, not labels with unequal chances.

lessons.title: Conditional probability
lessons.summary: Review joint events and fractions. A condition replaces the population in the denominator.

lessons.title: Bayes and base rates
lessons.summary: Review P(A given B): count A and B together, divided by the count of B.

lessons.title: Random variables and distributions
lessons.summary: Review weighted sums, squares and probability totals of 1. Algebra is recommended, not locked.

lessons.title: Probability in machine learning
lessons.summary: Review conditional probability, Bayes, and natural logarithms. No model-training prerequisites are required.

lessons.title: Independent Probability mastery
lessons.summary: 24 items, 80% and all critical gates; deterministic alternate retry.

modules.title: Algebra, Functions and Graphs
modules.summary: Equations, functions, graph interpretation, exponential/log behavior and composition.

lessons.title: Variables and equations
lessons.summary: A delivery costs a fixed fee plus a charge per kilometre. We need a rule to predict the bill—and to recover the distance from a known bill.

lessons.title: Functions, domains and outputs
lessons.summary: A pricing tool must return one defined quote for each permitted input. We must say which inputs it accepts before trusting its outputs.

lessons.title: Graphs, slopes and intercepts
lessons.summary: Two straight-line pricing rules can look similar. A graph lets us separate the starting fee from the cost of one extra unit.

lessons.title: Powers, growth and the number e
lessons.summary: A storage bill may add a fixed amount each day, while replicated data can multiply. These changes require different predictions.

lessons.title: Logarithms undo exponentials
lessons.summary: If a quantity has multiplied many times, we may want to recover how many multiplications happened. Logs let us describe multiplicative scales additively.

lessons.title: Transformations and composition
lessons.summary: A useful model may need a curved input relationship. We can change a familiar graph or connect two simple functions without treating every curve as a new mystery.

lessons.title: Independent Algebra assessment
lessons.summary: Demonstrate Algebra understanding independently of lesson completion.

experiments.title: Powers, growth and the number e experiment

modules.title: Calculus continuity and multivariable essentials
modules.summary: Completes the practical Calculus sequence alongside the preserved Derivatives pilot; full accessibility acceptance remains open.

lessons.title: Calculus essential extension
lessons.summary: Continuity/corners, partials, gradients and introductory sensitivity matrices on the original route.

modules.title: Linear Algebra
modules.summary: Core vector/matrix computations, geometric transformations, independent directions, undo and introductory eigen/PCA intuition.

lessons.title: Transformations, span and undo
lessons.summary: Map a plane, compare composition, explore independent directions and distinguish invertibility from stable undo.

lessons.title: Eigenvector and PCA intuition
lessons.summary: Known preserved lines, signed/zero eigenvalues and bounded covariance/PCA intuition.

lessons.title: Linear Algebra module assessment v2
lessons.summary: Core plus geometry, without silently upgrading old core evidence.

lessons.title: Vectors and dot products
lessons.summary: Magnitude, direction, addition, scaling, projections and feature alignment.

lessons.title: Matrices and multiplication
lessons.summary: Dataset axes, rectangular products, row-column calculation and schema diagnosis.

lessons.title: Independent Linear Algebra core assessment
lessons.summary: 16 questions across four core competencies; geometry extension excluded.

experiments.title: Vector and dot-product explorer with existing house lab
Rectangular batch explorer with existing matrix lab

modules.title: Derivatives pilot
modules.summary: Preserved scalar-derivative pilot; paired with Calculus essentials. Full accessibility acceptance remains open.

lessons.title: Why derivatives exist
lessons.summary: Distinguish average from instantaneous change and connect local rate to ML loss.

lessons.title: Secants & tangent lines
lessons.summary: Connect average change to instantaneous change.

lessons.title: Derivative rules
lessons.summary: Choose and explain common derivative rules.

lessons.title: Guided practice
lessons.summary: Interpret, calculate, and apply derivatives.

lessons.title: Interactive Derivative Lab
lessons.summary: Compare graphical, analytical, and numerical slopes.

lessons.title: Debugging derivatives in ML
lessons.summary: Find and repair a chain-rule error.

lessons.title: Mastery assessment
lessons.summary: Transfer understanding to unfamiliar examples.

modules.title: Linear Regression
modules.summary: Prediction, evaluation, optimization, implementation, and limitations.

lessons.title: Why Linear Regression Exists
lessons.summary: Explore a small house-price dataset and reason about a prediction before seeing an equation.

lessons.title: From Intuition to Equation
lessons.summary: Connect a line on a graph to its numerical prediction and then extend the idea to multiple inputs.

lessons.title: Measuring Prediction Errors
lessons.summary: Inspect prediction misses and predict which parameter change should improve the model.

lessons.title: How Gradient Descent Learns
lessons.summary: Step through training and connect each parameter movement to a change in dataset MSE.

lessons.title: Multiple Linear Regression
lessons.summary: Add and remove controlled features while preserving interpretable calculations.

lessons.title: Implementing the Algorithm
lessons.summary: Complete deterministic code exercises and compare the result with scikit-learn.

lessons.title: When Linear Regression Fails
lessons.summary: Investigate deliberately problematic datasets and choose a defensible next action.

lessons.title: Real-World Application
lessons.summary: Inspect data, select features, train, evaluate, and communicate model decisions.

lessons.title: Independent Mastery Challenge
lessons.summary: Demonstrate conceptual, applied, and independent competence without an upfront walkthrough.
